- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 20–40% for negative sentiment.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 2–3 day lag filter to smooth out immediate overshoots.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion in early periods; apply a 10–15% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative streak, model tends to overcorrect; cap forecast growth at 50% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates long-term (15+ day) price trajectories when sentiment is stable; add 10–20% buffer for sustained neutral sentiment.
- Avoid forecasting spikes in sentiment-driven periods without confirming historical correlation; use sentiment volatility as a multiplier (e.g., 1.2x for high volatility).
